title: Defend: write-before-ioctl for KEY_IMPORT avoids large kernel stack frames
description: crypto2dev_fd.c / crypto2dev_ioctl.h — key material for KEY_IMPORT is delivered via write() into inbuf, not embedded in the ioctl struct. The ioctl struct carries only metadata (algo, provider, key_type, keylen). A reviewer might suggest 'just put the key bytes in the ioctl struct like other ioctls do for their data'. This is wrong for two reasons: (1) worst-case key size is ML-DSA-87 at 4896 bytes, currently padded to KEY_IMPORT_MAXLEN=8192 for headroom; embedding this in an ioctl struct places 8192 bytes on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call (even for a 32-byte EC key), violating the kernel's ~1KB stack frame guideline and causing stack overflow risk; (2) the write-before-ioctl pattern allocates exactly inbuf_len bytes on the heap, zeroizes via memzero_explicit, and frees after import — minimal exposure. CLAUDE.md §5 documents this design decision explicitly.
